name: Stone Town, Zanzibar
tagline: A maze of coral-stone alleys, carved doors, spice markets and sultans' palaces on the Swahili coast.
highlight: Getting lost in the lanes, then watching the sun set over the harbour from a rooftop.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed Swahili trading port with Omani, Indian, Arab and European influences, famous for carved doors, markets, palaces and seafood.
metaDescription: A Stone Town travel guide: carved doors, House of Wonders, Forodhani Gardens, Old Fort, slave market memorial, spice tours, where to stay, costs and a two-day plan.

intro: Stone Town is the old heart of Zanzibar City, a tangle of narrow alleys, coral-stone houses and bustling bazaars. For centuries it was a trading hub for spices, ivory and, darkly, enslaved people, and its architecture mixes Swahili, Arab, Indian and European styles. The whole district is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The best way to see it is to walk without a plan. Look for the ornate carved wooden doors, studded with brass spikes, and for the balconied merchant houses. The House of Wonders, the Old Fort, the Anglican cathedral on the former slave market and the Sultan's Palace Museum all tell parts of the story, and at dusk the Forodhani Gardens fill with food stalls.

Zanzibar is also famed for its spices, and half-day spice farm tours from town are popular. Stone Town is the main base for catching ferries and flights to other islands, so most visitors spend two nights here before heading to the beaches. Dress modestly, since the population is largely Muslim.

whyVisit.intro: Stone Town is one of the most atmospheric historic towns in East Africa.

points.title: A living old town
points.text: Not a museum, people live and trade here.

bestTime.headline: June-October
bestTime.summary: The dry season from June to October is the best time, with the hottest months in January and February.
bestTime.avoid: April and May, during the long rains.
